applied.problem: Calls 'a hotter thing holds more energy' wrong in general, though it holds for the same mass and material; the cup and tank example also loses its 20 °C room on a dossier card. The latent-heat step misses freezing and condensing when cooling.
Says water at 0 °C or 100 °C takes in energy with no rise at all, but liquid water at 0 °C warms as soon as the ice has gone; only melting ice and boiling water hold steady.
Says all the heater's energy goes into the beaker, then that a real heater warms the beaker too; the model puts it all into the ice and water.
